headline: Level Designer
intro: I design spaces that teach players how to play them. Readable layouts, paced encounters, and systems that let a map keep changing after the player has learned it. These are the projects where the level and world design carried the experience.

bullets: Designed the interior room layout and the exterior station scenes
Built the space around a swivel-chair workstation loop, so every station stays reachable and readable from one seat
Tuned the environment for an eerie tone that keeps players second-guessing their decisions
Built the scenery for two worlds plus the main menu scene in a two-week jam
Made the main menu a playable 3D space rather than a flat screen, with UI living inside the world
Designed multiple puzzles that are solved through the environment itself
Created a map system that reshapes the layout as the game progresses, so a map keeps posing new problems
Designed around player-placed traps and walls, with enemies that re-route in real time
Shipped six evolving map designs supporting 14+ trap types
Designed the map layout for a large low-poly world built to run in a browser
Balanced open traversal against the performance budget of a web build
Placed items procedurally with a spawner that conforms to terrain geometry
Built a Garry's Mod map for Trouble in Terrorist Town, from scratch in the Hammer Editor
Shaped areas around player tendencies, funnelling people into shared spaces to create encounters
Built modular puzzle pieces designed for reuse across levels
Authored a visual editor guide to speed up map creation
Sequenced mechanics so each one is taught before it is combined with the next
